overall: The AG found one improper email deliberation by the ZBA outside a posted meeting and inaccurate minutes for three meetings, but no private meetings; ordered immediate compliance, email release, and minutes amendments.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the ZBA and Conservation Commission held 'private meetings' about a permit applicant's property; the AG found the discussions occurred in posted meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Because the informal conversations occurred during properly noticed meetings which were open to the public, we find that the ZBA and Commission did not deliberate outside of a posted meeting and did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Review of emails found a ZBA email chain about a site visit in which one member expressed an opinion on the matter, reaching a quorum outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: In the course of our review of emails to investigate whether the ZBA or Commission had held any meetings that were not posted and open to the public, we identified one email chain that constituted improper deliberation, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Town destroyed evidence of wrongdoing; the AG said even if true it would not violate the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Town failed to respond to requests for meeting minutes and audio recordings; these fell under the Public Records Law, outside OML jurisdiction.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, the Open Meeting Law does not govern a public body’s obligation to respond to requests for audio recordings, which fall under the Public Records Law, G.L. c. 66, § 10.

allegations.summary: Not alleged: the AG found approved minutes for two ZBA meetings and one Commission meeting omitted later informal discussion of an application, making them inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we find that the meeting minutes of the ZBA’s August 28, 2019, and November 20, 2019, meetings and the Commission’s January 21, 2020, meeting failed to include an accurate summary of the discussions held during those meetings, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law by the ZBA, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
Publicly release the three January 7-8, 2020, emails within 30 days, by reading them at a meeting and listing them in minutes, or posting them with the minutes on the municipal website.
Amend the ZBA and Commission meeting minutes within 60 days to include the omitted informal conversations, then send copies to the complainant and make them public within 65 days.
remedy_passage: We order the ZBA’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the ZBA that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
